title: On-device LLM plugin protocol - personal draft
content:
Personal scratchpad: exploring a lightweight plugin protocol for on-device LLM adapters

Purpose / motivation:
- Let third-party or partner components run a local model or accelerator and expose it to Redwood-hosted apps with a minimal handshake.
- Preserve privacy: model inputs can stay on-device while Redwood routes requests and collects anonymized telemetry.
- Keep runtime semantics (streaming, cache hints, kv-cache reuse) consistent so app code doesn't need to change per deployment mode.

Design constraints (rough):
- Tiny binary/JSON handshake. Must work over Unix domain sockets, loopback TLS, or gRPC on mobile.
- Capability advertising (max_seq_len, supported_quant, streaming, batched_invoke).
- Backwards-compatible: plugin must declare version and fallback profile.
- Security: mutual auth (mTLS or signed token) and whitelistable operations.

High-level flow (sketch):
1) Plugin starts, opens socket or registers to local discovery (mdns / systemd socket).
2) Redwood runtime (or local agent) performs handshake -> /v1/plugin/register (capabilities + signed attestation).
3) Runtime maps model id -> local plugin if policies allow.
4) App request arrives, runtime selects route: plugin (on-device) or remote hosted.
5) Plugin invoked with unified invoke payload; plugin streams tokens back or returns final response.
6) Runtime applies tracing / billing hooks, optionally performs fallback if plugin fails.

ASCII arch diagram:

  [App] --(Redwood SDK)--> [Local Agent / Runtime] --(Plugin protocol)--> [On-device Plugin (model)]
       |                                         |--(control plane telemetry)-> [Redwood Control Plane]
       v                                         \--(fallback)-> [Hosted Redwood Model Pool]

Core API shapes (very rough):

1) POST /v1/plugin/register\Request body (JSON):
{
  "plugin_id": "device-uuid-abc",
  "plugin_version": "0.3.1",
  "models": [
    {"name": "llama2-13b-q8", "max_seq": "8192", "quant": "q8_0", "capabilities": ["streaming","batch"]}
  ],
  "signing_key": "base64(pubkey)",
  "attestation": "tpm-sig-or-jwt"
}

Server returns: 200 OK + {"accepted": true, "profile_id": "on-device-llama2-q8", "routing_priority": "local-first"}

Notes: need to keep this small. Consider compressed CBOR variant for binary handshake.

2) POST /v1/plugin/invoke (or gRPC stream)\Request body (JSON):
{
  "profile_id": "on-device-llama2-q8",
  "request_id": "r-123",
  "prompt": "<string or token ids>",
  "max_tokens": 512,
  "temperature": 0.2,
  "kv_cache_hint": "reuse-session-42",
  "input_mode": "text|tokens",
  "client_metadata": {"sdk_version": "rdw-js-1.8.0"}
}

Response: supports streaming SSE / chunked gRPC where each event is:
{ "type": "delta", "tokens": "...", "logprob": null, "cursor": 123 }

Control semantics to agree on:
- kv_cache_hint: opaque token provided by runtime to let plugin persist last kv cache; helps prefix reuse across restarts.
- cache_ttl: how long plugin may reuse cached prefetched activations.
- routing_policy: "local-first", "cost-preference", "latency-first". Plugin can optionally advertise cost_metric (ops/sec) so runtime can compare.

Configuration sketch (YAML-style, for local agent):
agent:
  plugin_discovery:
    - unix_socket: /var/run/rdw/plugin.sock
    - mdns: rdw-plugins.local
  security:
    mTLS: true
    allowed_plugins:
      - plugin_id: device-uuid-abc
        owner: "device-owner"
  routing_overrides:
    - model_alias: "gpt-lite"
      map_to: "on-device-llama2-q8"
      fallback: "hosted/gpt4-mini"

Open questions / TODOs:
- How do we handle model updates on-device? push from control plane or pull by plugin? need atomic replacement without breaking kv cache semantics.
- Billing: local execution shouldn't bill token usage? or should it record anonymized counters for cost reporting? need legal guidance.
- Attestation: define minimal attestation schema for enterprise customers (HSM/Tee options).
- Performance signals: define cost_metric (ms/token, p50/p95, ops/watt) and a standard microbenchmark harness for plugins.
- Migration story: how apps declare they can accept on-device route (feature flag) vs forcing hosted.

Edge cases / failure modes:
- Plugin returns malformed stream: runtime should abort and optionally try fallback with request duplication idempotency.
- Plugin crash mid-stream: resume from last stable token? likely impossible without shared kv cache; fall back to hosted generation starting from prompt+generated prefix (deduping required).
- Privacy leak: plugin may try to call out to network. agent must enforce egress rules (network namespace or sandbox).

Notes to self: keep this document terse. Next steps:
- Prototype a tiny Go agent that accepts unix socket registration and forwards a simple prompt. Use llama.cpp plugin binary toy.
- Add minimal integrity check (signed manifest).
- Create RFC draft for team review (link to GH issue above).

References / links I might need to paste into RFC:
- GH RFC notes: redwood-inference/rfcs#214 (stub)
- Example attestation spec: https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-cicp/ (placeholder)
- Prior art: VS Code Extension Host handshake, Kubernetes device plugins.

Quick checklist for prototype:
- [ ] Unix socket discovery + register flow
- [ ] Basic invoke + streaming demo (node client -> local plugin -> node client)
- [ ] Fallback behavior test (simulate plugin crash)
- [ ] Policy test: restrict network egress from plugin process
- [ ] Document minimal telemetry (p50, p95, tokens_executed)

-- end personal scratchpad --

(rough, messy — meant for quick iteration; will probably split into two RFCs: protocol + security/attestation)
